expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "> **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**"

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Has bold section labels "Key debates", "Major voices", "Patterns" and "Open questions".

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: By estimate, the four sections come to about 350–420 words, which is inside the 300–500 range.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map of six possible angles to: .../mind-map.html". The file defines `const DATA = {...}` from the template.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says there are "six possible angles". Each visible branch has 2–3 children, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1, e.g. "saturation": 0.8 and "saturation": 0.15. The file is cut off, so the last branches can't be fully checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short topics, for example "Academic achievement", "Budgets and cost savings" and "Meals and food access". None is phrased as a question.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you most, and why?" The reply recommends no angle.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: The links to educationnext, edweek 2026/04, edweek 2025/07, news.uoregon and chalkbeat were all fetched with WebFetch. RAND, ECS and Stateline were left out: "wouldn't open, so I left them out".

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you most, and why?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: There are exactly two questions: "what do you think about four-day weeks right now..." and "which direction pulls you most, and why?"
